newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of Italy in EMU edge up - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of Italy in EMU edge up - JP Morgan.

text.p: Expectations that Italy will be a founding member of European economic and monetary union (EMU) grew in the past week but the likelihood of Spain and Portugal joining from the outset slipped, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed on Friday.

There is a 71 percent chance of Italy joining a core group of countries in launching the planned single European currency, according to JP Morgan's "EMU calculator," which is derived from the interest-rate swaps market. That is up from a 67 percent reading for Italy a week ago.
The probability of France and Belgium joining Germany in monetary union on schedule in 1999 was unchanged from last week at 100 percent.

Spain and Portugal's perceived chance of entering EMU slipped marginally, however. The probability that Spain will join EMU at the outset was at 79 percent on Friday, down from 80 percent a week ago, while Portugal's chances dipped to 78 percent from 80 percent.

Britain, already viewed as the least likely country to join Germany in EMU of the 10 ranked by the EMU Calculator, saw this probability fall further. Its hopes of EMU membership in 1999 are given a 34 percent rating, down from 38 percent last week.
JP Morgan said there was a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of less than five percentage points on average.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
